title: Enhancing Contrastive Learning on Graphs with Node Similarity

problem.claim: Many graph neural networks require labeled data, which is challenging to obtain.

gap.claim: Existing graph contrastive learning methods may be sub-optimal because they have limited positive samples and may select false-negative samples.

contributions.claim: The study proposes an enhanced objective for graph contrastive learning that addresses limited positive samples and false-negative samples.
The authors introduce an ideal objective using all positive and no false-negative samples, then transform it probabilistically according to sampling distributions.
The authors model the sampling distributions with node similarity and derive an enhanced objective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report comprehensive experiments showing the effectiveness of the proposed enhanced objective across a broad set of graph contrastive learning models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph neural networks have been successful for graph-related tasks, but many require difficult-to-obtain labeled data.
Graph contrastive learning addresses the labeling challenge by contrasting similar and dissimilar nodes.
Current sampling practices can be sub-optimal because of limited positive samples and false-negative samples.
The study develops an enhanced objective through an ideal objective, probabilistic transformation, and node-similarity modeling, then reports comprehensive experiments across a broad set of models.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the evaluated datasets, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not specify the graph contrastive learning models included in the experiments.
The abstract does not provide implementation or sampling details.
The abstract does not state limitations or failure cases.
